prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. Positions are fractions of image width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. One frame of a slow camera move in a Nordic girl's room at a child's eye height, turned to face the desk wall square-on. 24 mm shift lens at 1.0 m, level, straight verticals, all sharp. The window is out of frame on the left; the bed's foot is cut at the lower left; the desk stands left of centre; the room's corner is at x 0.60 and the right 40 % of the frame is the near wall.

SCALE: the clay is also the size of everything. Every wall, the corner, every skirting line and piece of fixed furniture stays exactly where the clay draws it and exactly as large: the 90 x 50 cm oak desk spans x 0.22-0.475, its top at y 0.585-0.627, its legs to y 0.95; the foot of the 96 x 196 cm oak bed spans x 0.00-0.18 from y 0.625 to the bottom edge; the room's corner is the vertical line at x 0.60; the band's top is level with the lower ledge at y 0.36. Never enlarge or shrink a piece to match a cut-out (they come from the same spot turned 33 degrees left); if a piece looks wrong in size, keep the clay's size.

CUT-OUTS. Images 1-5 are cut-outs of a photograph of this room from this spot turned toward the window: materials, colours and light only, never framing, position or scale (1 desk, doll, band, skirting, planks; 2 the prints; 3 the ledges; 4 bed foot and muslin; 5 upper wall and the band line). Images 6-9 are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture.

2. LIGHT. One key: soft north winter daylight from the window out of frame on the left, no sun. No lamp is lit. The desk wall takes it from the left and falls off half a stop toward the corner; the near wall faces the window: calm, even light, a touch darker toward the right edge, no hot spot. Every piece: a lit left face, a shadow side a stop darker; the desk casts a long soft shadow right and toward the camera; dense contact shadows. Exposed for white: the upper walls clean white. Real contrast, never milky. 4600 K: the white stays white, never cream, pink, yellow or grey; the blush never bleeds into it.

3. MATERIALS. Upper walls matte mineral paint #F4F1EC. On the desk wall only: a crisp blush-clay band #E8D5CC to 1.25 m, its top level with the lower ledge at y 0.36, with a blush skirting; band and skirting stop in a clean vertical line at the corner, x 0.60. The near wall on the right is all warm white #F4F1EC with a warm-white skirting, no band. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E, the same planks as cut-out 1. Bed and desk: oiled oak #C8A27A, satin sheen, a soft highlight along the desk top.

4. PRODUCTS, one per line, each on its clay placeholder and each the same object as in its cut-out:
a. PRINTS above the desk, x 0.33-0.48, y 0.15-0.31: the two framed charcoal flower-silhouette prints of cut-out 2, thin light frames.
b. LEDGES at the left edge, x 0.00-0.15, y 0.11-0.37: the two tiers of face-out oak ledges with picture books in blush, oat and warm white of cut-out 3, no readable text, cut by the left edge.
e. BLANKET on the bed foot, lower left, x 0.00-0.12, y 0.65-0.71: the folded beige muslin of cut-out 4.
i. DOLL at the desk's left end, x 0.29-0.33, y 0.48-0.59: the 35 cm linen bunny doll in the oat dress of cut-out 1, sitting against the wall; the rest of the desk bare.

5. NOT IN FRAME: window, blind or curtain, any lamp, chair, doll pram, pen cup, other toys, rug, basket, clothes, door, switch, socket, cable, text, people. No snow anywhere. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, halos, HDR, grain or vignette.
